messages:
mia (product): quick question — for the rollouts console card labelled 'Automatic fallback', should the default mode be 'degrade' or 'failover'? early alpha testers are mixing up what each option does.
alex (eng-platform): imo default = 'failover with audit' so we don't silently return degraded outputs. users expect continuity.
ravi (eng-runtime): important distinction: a 'degrade' can mean model-variant substitution (quantized model) or response truncation. 'Failover' is routing to a different endpoint/region. must call out both behaviors in the UI.
taylor (sre): telemetry requirement: whenever auto-fallback triggers, log trigger_reason, selected_fallback, pre/post latency, and model hashes. retention depends on tier but store raw events for 90d at least.
mia (product): propose we expose three explicit modes in the UI: 1) Graceful degrade — swap to compatible variant and attempt to preserve shape; 2) Failover — route to alternate endpoint/region; 3) Circuit-breaker — reject + optional cached response. show short descriptions inline.
alex (eng-platform): UX idea — add small 'simulate' button next to mode that runs a dry-run over a sample workload and shows predicted audit events. also require explicit opt-in for any 'silent degrade' that omits user-visible warning (legal/compliance).
ravi (eng-runtime): example policy we expect from console -> API (JSON):
```json
{
  "mode": "graceful_degrade",
  "trigger": {"error_rate": 0.05, "latency_p95_ms": 800},
  "fallback": {"type": "model_variant", "id": "rw:v1-quant"},
  "audit": {"enabled": true, "sample_rate": 0.1}
}
```
taylor (sre): audit log fields we need: trace_id, request_tokens, trigger_metric, fallback_id, from_model_hash, to_model_hash, region, timestamp, actor_type (automated/manual). also capture a small request/response sample for QA (scrubbed).
mia (product): defaults thinking: audit.enabled = true, sample_rate = 0.05 for hosted plans; enterprise toggle to 1.0 if data_classification.PII = true. make that visible on the policy card.
alex (eng-platform): add hysteresis controls in the UI to prevent oscillation: cooldown_secs, min_requests_window, min_consecutive_triggers. show a small tooltip explaining why. example: cooldown_secs=300, min_requests=1000.
ravi (eng-runtime): one more API/field naming callout — backend uses "contingency" currently while console copy says "fallback_policy". we should standardize on "contingency" in the API and map UI labels to friendly text to avoid confusion in infra logs.
mia (product): agree — keep user-facing label 'fallback' but map to API field contingency. will add mapping note to docs. :thumbsup: 
deploy-bot: deploy status: merged autofallback-ux branch -> staging, feature flag autofallback_console_sim:off
taylor (sre): i'll draft the runbook and telemetry schema tomorrow (assigning to myself). also will add checklist for manual rollback if auto-fallback repeatedly triggers.
mia (product): thanks — next steps: alex can you mock the card copy and simulate button, ravi can you add API mapping and sample payload to the spec, taylor please add telemetry schema + runbook. i'll consolidate docs and update product PR.
alex (eng-platform): will do. expect mock by EOW.
ravi (eng-runtime): i'll update API spec and include mapping examples.
taylor (sre): adding runbook notes to the incidents repo after mock review.
mia (product): cool, closing this thread — we'll review in weekly rollouts sync.
